name: Do I need an architect or structural engineer for an open-floor-plan conversion?

mainEntity.name: Do I need an architect or structural engineer for an open-floor-plan conversion?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, for most open-floor-plan conversions, especially those involving load-bearing walls, you will need the expertise of both an architect and a structural engineer. An architect helps design the new layout and ensures aesthetic appeal and functionality. A structural engineer assesses the integrity of your home, determines if walls are load-bearing, and designs the necessary supports (like beams) to maintain structural stability and comply with building codes. This ensures safety and proper execution.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, an architect and structural engineer are often necessary, especially for load-bearing walls, to ensure design, safety, and code compliance.
